title: Two independent origins, one self-revising source line — the case the naive rule gets wrong
role: hard case; forces the versioned contradiction and recency rules to be decided explicitly
_pre_registration: Selected on evidence quality only. The pool's price path inside the replay window was deliberately NOT inspected before this file was frozen.
_why_this_exists: Scenario A is held at WATCH by the single-origin rule and scenario B is promoted by an official filing. Neither exercises the boundary where non-official evidence legitimately CAN promote. This scenario sits exactly on that boundary: two genuinely independent outlets, no official confirmation, and a source line that revised its own headline figure by more than 2x. Without it, T1.2 could ship a promotion rule that has never been tested against a real ambiguous input.

independenceSummary._significance: This clears the 'at least two genuinely independent evidence sources' bar in §0.7. If market confirmation is also fresh, the literal reading of the promotion rule permits PROTECT here with no official filing anywhere in sight.

preRegisteredExpectation._honesty: No outcome is asserted, because the correct answer depends on a rule that has not been written yet. Asserting WATCH now and then implementing whatever produces WATCH would be fitting the rule to the desired answer.
preRegisteredExpectation.openRuleQuestion: Does a source line that revised its own headline figure downward by more than 2x within 19 days count as self-contradicting for promotion purposes, and does that cap promotion at WATCH even when a second independent origin agrees on the direction of the story?

permittedOutcomes.requires: T1.2 decides that an unresolved self-revision of this magnitude, or the absence of any official confirmation, caps non-official promotion.

T1.2 decides two independent origins suffice, AND market confirmation is CONFIRMED and fresh at the anchor. In that case the bounded action must still respect the full fee ceiling, duration, cooldown and decay envelope.

preRegisteredExpectation.hardConstraint: Whichever branch T1.2 chooses, the rule must be frozen in versioned configuration BEFORE this scenario's market data is scored, and the same rule must apply unchanged to scenarios A, B and D.
preRegisteredExpectation.notPermitted: Choosing the rule after seeing which branch produces a better benchmark number.

_schemaChangeLog: 0.2.0 (T1.2): added `materiality` to every claim. T1.1 made materiality a separate axis from provenance, because an official filing is not automatically an LP-relevant corporate action. The engine treats a missing value as UNKNOWN and refuses to promote on it, so the field had to be stated rather than inferred.

ruleResolution.resolvedBefore: any market data for this scenario was scored
ruleResolution.openQuestion: Does a source line that revised its own headline figure downward by more than 2x within 19 days count as self-contradicting for promotion purposes, and does that cap promotion at WATCH even when a second independent origin agrees on the direction of the story?
ruleResolution.decision: A source line that has materially revised its own quantitative claim inside the evidence window may still support a WATCH, but may NOT be counted toward the two independent sources that non-official PROTECT requires. The disqualification applies to the whole independenceGroup, because a revision is a property of the source line, not of one article.
ruleResolution.reasoning: The two-source rule exists to establish that a fact is corroborated. A source that has demonstrably been wrong about the magnitude of that very fact within the window has not established the fact; it has established that the number is still moving. Acting on an unsettled number is exactly what bounded-action discipline is meant to prevent.
whyThisIsNotResultDriven: The rule is threshold-free — there is no ratio to tune, so it cannot be fitted to this scenario.
It is strictly conservative: it can only block promotion, never enable it, so it cannot manufacture a favourable benchmark result.
It generalises to the common pattern in breaking financial news, where an early figure is corrected within days.
It was frozen in code and tested before any market data for this window was scored.

nonSelectedBranch.note: Kept as a disclosed sensitivity per T0.4 §3. Test `scenario C would have promoted without the self-revision rule` demonstrates that removing the rule flips this scenario to PROTECT with 2 independent sources — which is what makes the rule load-bearing rather than incidental.
